diagnoses.summary: PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with both high Hotelling T2 and high SPE, dominated by the reactor pressure signal. Top contributing variable is CSTR pressure. Rule-based hints point to a problematic Hydrogen PCV (H2 PCV) affecting reactor pressure. The most consistent single fault is degradation or blockage in the H2 PCV (cstr_vent_valve).
High SPE with coherent T² rise suggests a PCV-related issue driving reactor pressure together with CSTR inlet controls. Rule-based hints point to H2 PCV anomalies as the root cause.

The PCA indicates a high SPE with coherent movement along multiple variables, dominated by the hydrogen vent/PCV related signals, pointing to a fault in the H2 PCV (valve) system causing abnormal reactor pressure behavior and compensatory control action.

PCA flags a strong SPE-driven abnormality with a coherent disturbance dominated by the H2 PCV control path and CSTR pressure signal; the data point to an H2 PCV fault (capacity degradation or stuck closed) as the primary cause of the upset.
PCA anomaly with large T² and SPE driven mainly by CSTR pressure signal and H2 vent (PCV) related variables; likely a PCV fault causing abnormal reactor pressure dynamics.

PCA detects a large, coherent plant upset with both T2 and SPE violated; strongest evidence points to H2 PCV (vent) related faults propagating pressure rise in the CSTR. Rule-based hints favor PCV issues over pure sensor drift.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations and a strongly dominant contribution from reactor pressure measurement and its pressure-control loop, consistent with H2 PCV (vent) faulting. Likely PCV actuator issue causing high reactor pressure and compensatory control action.

PCA signals a large, coherent plant upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations. The strongest contributing evidence points to the hydrogen PCV (cstr_vent_valve) being off-norm, driving reactor pressure up and triggering downstream effects. Sensor bias on reactor pressure is also plausible if measurements are skewed, but actuator faults at the PCV are more consistent with the dominant T2/SPE pattern.

PCA flags large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violating limits. The dominant driver is the reactor pressure-related signal (meas.cstr_pressure_bar) with the R_PIC loop output saturated off its setpoint, pointing toward a H2 PCV issue propagating through the system. The rule evidence points to H2 PCV faults (capacity degradation or sticking) as the primary cause, with secondary indications of sensor bias and an out-of-range PI output.

PCA flag shows a large, coherent process upset with strong reactor pressure indication and a saturated PID loop on the PI controller for the H2 PCV (R_PIC). The evidence points to an H2 PCV valve fault causing abnormal reactor pressure behavior and forcing the pressure loop to saturate.
Abnormal PCA with large coherent shift and simultaneous SPE violation. Most likely a fault in the H2 PCV (vent) causing reactor pressure control issues and loop saturation.
A large, coherent process upset with strong reactor pressure involvement and saturated control loops, consistent with a degraded or stuck hydrogen purge (PCV) valve affecting reactor pressure.

Both Hotelling T² and SPE are violated with a coherent plant upset, dominated by the reactor pressure signal and apparent PCV-driven control actions. Likely H2 PCV issue causing reactor pressure rise and sensor/controller interactions.

The PCA flags a large, global upset with both T² and SPE violated, dominated by the reactor side (cstr_pressure_bar) and with loop saturation on R_PIC and RB_LIC. The most consistent single cause is a H2 PCV issue propagating through the CSTR, supported by saturated control loops and the presence of DIST_X_L alarm implying distillation pressure/condensing issues linked to PCV behavior.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations and a prominent disturbance in reactor pressure control. The strongest evidence points to hydrogen PCV (pressure control valve) related faults propagating through the system, with additional support for condenser/heat removal inefficiencies and CSTR outlet issues.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with both T2 and SPE violated, dominated by a large contribution from reactor pressure (meas.cstr_pressure_bar). The evidence points to an H2 PCV related fault causing reactor pressure excursions and loop saturation.

The PCA signals a large, coherent plant upset dominated by CSTR pressure dynamics and loop saturation. The most plausible root cause is a fault in the H2 PCV (valve) system causing improper pressure relief, with secondary contributions from condenser cooling issues and related loop saturations.

The PCA detects a large coherent plant upset with both Hotelling T² and SPE violated, dominated by a reactor pressure/process disturbance. Given the heavy contribution from the CSTR pressure measurement and the saturated control loops around the H2 vent (PCV) and related pressure control, the disturbance is most consistent with H2 PCV degradation or obstruction, causing elevated reactor pressure and compensatory loop action. An additional but secondary contributor is condenser cooling loss affecting downstream separation (DIST_X_L), but this is less likely the root cause than PCV issues.

A large coherent process upset with strong reactor-related perturbations and an active distillation anomaly. The evidence points to condenser cooling and H2 vent issues, with possible PCV-related capacity/sticking faults contributing to the high SPE/T2. Likely multiple faults active: condenser cooling loss plus PCV-related valve issues.

The abnormal PCA signal is dominated by a large, coherent upset with reactor pressure-related measurements driving most of the deviation, accompanied by loop saturation upstream of the CSTR and abnormal distillate composition. The evidence points to an H2 vent (PCV) related fault causing pressure control issues, with condenser cooling loss also plausible as a secondary contributor.

High-dimensional PCA shows a large, coherent upset dominated by reactor pressure measurement and PCV-related control activity, with an ongoing condenser-related disturbance. The most consistent explanation is degradation or sticking of the H2 PCV (and associated control saturation), causing elevated reactor pressure and compensatory loop actions.

Both Hotelling T² and SPE are violated with coherent upset patterns, and the top contributors point to reactor pressure control/PCV-related issues and downstream distillation disturbances. The rules also flag saturated PI loops and possible PCV faults. Most likely cause is H2 PCV related faults causing process-wide coupling disruption, with secondary contributions from condenser/distillate disturbances.

PCA shows a large, coherent plant Move with both T² and SPE violated, dominated by a single measurement and supported by reactor/column control signals. The strongest diagnosed fault is degradation of the H2 PCV capacity, with additional risk of condenser cooling issues and related actuator constraints.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations and a strong contribution from the condenser path, along with a distillate composition alarm. The most consistent single fault is a loss of condenser cooling effectiveness causing elevated column pressure and related disturbances.
PCA detects a large, coherent process upset with both T2 and SPE violated. Evidence points to degraded condenser cooling effectiveness causing distillation disturbances and saturated control loops.

High process move with large SPE indicating a coherent upset, strongly driven by reactor/cstr pressure and top-stage variables, with multiple duty loop outputs saturated at their limits and a DIST_X_L alarm on distillate acetone. Likely a condenser cooling issue driving column pressure up, with possible H2 PCV degradation contributing to pressure rise and loop saturation.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous high T2 and high SPE, driven primarily by a major rise in measured CSTR pressure and related column/top conditions. Faults pointing to condenser cooling losses best explain the observed SPE and associated elevated tray temperatures and distillate alarm.

PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations, with the strongest rule-based indication pointing to reduced condenser cooling effectiveness leading to abnormal column behavior.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous high T² and SPE, dominated by a severe disturbance in the condenser cooling path and saturated control loops downstream of the CSTR/column. The most consistent fault is a loss of condenser cooling effectiveness causing elevated distillate heat load and triggering multiple valve/controller saturations and the DIST_X_L alarm.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with both high Hotelling T² and high SPE, indicating a major process disturbance with new/degraded correlations. Several loops are saturated and an acetone distillate alarm is active, pointing to a condenser-side disturbance propagating through the column. Leaks or valve/flow issues are less likely given the coherence of the upset, but some loop outputs are saturated at setpoint, suggesting upstream compensation limits are reached.

PCA flags a highly coherent, large plant upset with strong SPE anomalies and multiple saturated control loops, centered on the reflux drum region and CSTR inputs. The DR_L_LL alarm plus drum holdup behavior points to a drum-related leakage/withdrawal issue propagating through the CSTR feed and column system. Several loop outputs are saturated with PVs off setpoints, indicating loss of controller authority and a mass/energy imbalance driving the disturbance.
